facts.text: Calgary registers 221 head offices with 29,824 head office employees in 2024, according to Statistics Canada's Annual Head Office Survey.
The 2025 Calgary Stampede draws total attendance of 1,470,288, about 7,000 fewer than in 2024 and just short of the all-time record.
Calgary's labour force participation rate is 71.2 per cent, while the unemployment rate stands at 7.2 per cent amid rapid population growth.
The City of Calgary projects local economic growth of 2.4 per cent in 2026, with population growth and inflation both around two per cent.
In 2021 there were 177,405 Calgarians aged 65 and over, up 28 per cent from 138,405 in 2016, the fastest-growing age group in the city over 20 years.

overview: Calgary reached 1.3 million residents in the 2021 Census, up 5.5 per cent from 2016, and remains young for a major Canadian city with a median age of 38.0. Households reported a median total income of $98,000 in 2020, so there is real spending power across 502,301 occupied dwellings.

The city covers 820.62 square kilometres and hosts 221 head offices, so business customers and consumers are both plentiful but widely dispersed. A local business is rarely the only option, which makes visibility in specific quadrants and communities more valuable than citywide reach.

byService.lead-generation: Lead generation in Calgary should segment by quadrant and by buyer type, since 1.3 million residents and 221 head offices create very different sales conversations across 820.62 square kilometres.
byService.seo: In a city of 1.3 million with thousands of competing firms, Calgary SEO must win community-level and service-specific searches rather than generic city terms.
byService.website-development: A Calgary website should convert a mobile-first audience with a median age of 38.0 and household incomes of $98,000, which means fast pages, online booking and transparent pricing.
byService.branding: Because Calgary added 5.5 per cent more residents between 2016 and 2021, branding should welcome newcomers who are still forming loyalties while staying credible with head-office buyers.
